workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§242–244
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§242–244: The Sharing Out of the People and the Quarrel with Qasar
part: §§242–244 — The Sharing Out of the People and the Quarrel with Qasar
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§242–244, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Chinggis Qahan shares the people out among his mother, his sons and his brothers, and Mother is given Ödchigin's share (§242); he names the stewards set over each household and says of Cha'adai that he is firm and fine-tempered and that Kökösös is to stay near and speak his thoughts (§243); then Teb-Tenggeri, one of the seven sons of Münlig, stirs the Qahan against his brother Qasar, and Mother comes through the night to free Qasar and rebuke her son (§244). Grammar to watch: the dative-locative endings that the Ming glossators write 行 ("to"), the converb chains in -žu/-žü that carry the action, the reflexive-possessives -jan/-jen that Shiratori prints with a bracketed linking vowel (γal(i)-jan, kököd(i)-jen), and the quotations, where Shiratori's marks are partial and the notes say where `i` supplies one.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolžu "eke-de köġüd-te deġü-ner-e irge qubijažu ögüje keġen ögürün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to become; with žarliγ, “to make (a decree)” [做着]
dative-locative: to, at (front-vowel form, after d)
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]
to divide, share out (stem inferred from the Ming 分) [分着]
hortative: let us … (first person plural, front-vowel form)

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan decree making, "mother-to, sons-to, younger-brothers-to people dividing, let-us-give saying, giving-when:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan issued a decree, saying, “Let us divide the people and give them to Mother, to the sons, to the younger brothers.” And when he gave them out, he said:
sentences.n: Read bolžu 'making' with žarliγ 'decree' (Ming 聖旨 + 做着): the pair means 'issuing a decree', as elsewhere. The three datives eke-de, köġüd-te, deġü-ner-e are 'to the mother, to the sons, to the younger brothers' (Ming 行 each time); qubijažu 'dividing' is a converb that waits for ögüje 'let us give' (-üje, the first-person hortative, Ming 與咱), and keġen 'saying' closes the quotation. Shiratori prints an opening mark at eke-de but no closing mark before ögürün (-rün, 'when giving'); `i` supplies the closing mark after keġen. The stem qubija- is inferred from the Ming 分 'divide'. The colon leads into the speech that opens at Ulus.

sentences.t: "Ulus qurijaγ̇an žobaγsad eke buju-že.

morph.gloss: to gather, bring together (stem inferred from the Ming 收拾 “collect, put in order”) [收拾]
to toil, suffer hardship (stem inferred from the Ming 辛苦) [辛苦了的每]
past participle, plural: those who have …ed (Ming 每)
to be (stem bu- before -ju; inferred from the Ming 有) [有 也者︀]

sentences.l: "People gathering, toiling-ones, mother is.
sentences.i: “As for those who toiled to gather the people, there is Mother.
sentences.n: A list in three beats, each ending in the verb 'is' with the particle -že (Ming 也者): the one who did the work, the eldest son, the youngest brother. qurijaγ̇an (Ming 收拾 'collect, put in order') and žobaγsad (Ming 辛苦了的每 'those who toiled') have stems inferred from the Ming alone; žobaγsad is a plural participle, which is why I write 'those who toiled' and let Mother stand as the one named. buju-že is bü- 'be' with an ending I read as -ju (the present, as in bijü); that reading is uncertain, but the Ming 有 'is' fixes the sense. Opening quotation mark is Shiratori's on Ulus; the speech runs to bi-že" two units on.

sentences.t: Köġüd-ün min-u aqa Žüči bi-že.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant)
my, of me (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
elder brother; here “eldest” (Ming 長), the noun used as an adjective [長]
to be (stem bi- before -že) [有 也者︀]

sentences.l: Sons-of my eldest Žüči is.
sentences.i: Of my sons there is the eldest, Jüchi.
sentences.n: Köġüd-ün is köġün 'son' + plural -d + genitive -ün, 'of the sons'; min-u 'my' follows the genitive köġüd-ün it belongs to, and aqa, which the Ming glosses 長 'eldest', is the noun 'elder brother' used as an adjective (as in earlier parts). The verb is bi-že 'is indeed', the same shape as buju-že above.

sentences.t: Deġü-ner-ün min-u nilqa Ödčigin bi-že"

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant)
my, of me (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
young, small, the youngest (Ming 最少) [最少]

sentences.l: Younger-brothers-of my youngest Ödčigin is"
sentences.i: Of my younger brothers there is the youngest, Ödchigin.”
sentences.n: The parallel to the last unit: Deġü-ner-ün 'of the younger brothers' (deġü + plural -ner + genitive -ün), nilqa 'the youngest' (Ming 最少). The closing quotation mark is printed on bi-že here, and closes the speech that opened at Ulus; the first quote, opened at eke-de, has no closing mark in Shiratori (see the first unit).

sentences.t: keġežü eke-de Ödčigin-ü qubi kiġed tümen irge ögbe.

morph.gloss: and, and the others (Ming 等) [等]
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]

sentences.l: Saying, mother-to Ödčigin-of share and ten-thousand people gave.
sentences.i: Having said this, he gave Mother the share of Ödchigin and ten thousand people.
sentences.n: keġežü 'saying' picks up the speech just ended. eke-de is 'to the mother' (Ming 行), Ödčigin-ü the genitive 'of Ödchigin', qubi 'share' (Ming 分子) and kiġed 'and' (Ming 等, which also means 'and so on'); tümen is a ten-thousand, and ögbe is the past of ög- 'give'. Doubtful: kiġed may join two gifts, 'the share and ten thousand people', or may mean 'the share, namely ten thousand people' (compare §243, where Chinggis says he gave ten thousand people to Mother and Ödchigin); `i` keeps the plain 'and', and the text only says that this went to Mother.

sentences.t: Eke čimadčü ese doṅγodba.

morph.gloss: to find fault, blame; here, from the Ming 嫌少 “dislike as too little”, to find too little (stem as the glossary’s čimadba) [嫌少着]
to make a sound, utter (stem inferred from the Ming 作聲) [作聲了]

sentences.l: Mother finding-too-little, not made-a-sound.
sentences.i: Mother thought it too little, but she did not utter a sound.
sentences.n: čimadčü is a converb in -čü, with a stem čimad- inferred from the Ming 嫌少 'dislike as too little'; doṅγodba is the past of doṅγod-, 'to make a sound', again inferred from the Ming 作聲 'make a noise'. ese (Ming 不曾) negates a past action. So she found it too little yet kept silent; the Ming does not say why, and I leave it at that.

sentences.t: Žüči-de jesün miṅγad irge ögbe.

morph.gloss: nine (the Ming here writes 九十 “ninety”; the Mongol word is “nine”) [九十]
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]

sentences.l: Žüči-to nine thousands people gave.
sentences.i: To Jüchi he gave nine thousand people.
sentences.n: Žüči-de is 'to Jüchi' (Ming 行). miṅγad is 'thousand' + plural -d (Ming 千每 'thousands'), so a number before it counts thousands. Doubtful: jesün is the ordinary word for 'nine', but the Ming writes 九十 'ninety' here; I follow the Mongol word, 'nine thousand', and flag that the Ming glossators seem to have read it as 'ninety (thousand)'.

sentences.t: Čaγ̇adaj-a naiman miṅγad irge ögbe.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to (back-vowel form; written -aj-a with a glide j)
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]

sentences.l: Čaγ̇adai-to eight thousands people gave.
sentences.i: To Cha'adai he gave eight thousand people.
sentences.n: Čaγ̇adaj-a is the name Čaγ̇adai plus dative-locative -a, with a glide j written between (Ming 人名行 'to the man'). The names in these gifts take a dative ending in -a or -e, mostly following the stem's vowel harmony (Tolui, two units on, is the exception). naiman is 'eight'.

sentences.t: Ögödej-e tabun miṅγad irge ögbe.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to (front-vowel form; written -ej-e with a glide j)
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]

sentences.l: Ögödei-to five thousands people gave.
sentences.i: To Ögödei he gave five thousand people.
sentences.n: Ögödej-e is Ögödei + dative-locative -e (front-vowel form after the glide j), 'to Ögödei'. tabun is 'five'; the Ming counts it 千每 'thousands'.

sentences.t: Toluj-a tabun miṅγad irge ögbe.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to (written Toluj-a with a glide j)
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]

sentences.l: Tolui-to five thousands people gave.
sentences.i: To Tolui he gave five thousand people.
sentences.n: Toluj-a is Tolui + dative-locative -a (the back-vowel form written even after Tolui's front stem, as Shiratori prints it, with the glide j). Same frame as the last two units.

sentences.t: Qasar-a dörben miṅγad irge ögbe.

morph.gloss: Qasar, a man’s name [人名 行]
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]

sentences.l: Qasar-to four thousands people gave.
sentences.i: To Qasar he gave four thousand people.
sentences.n: Qasar-a is the name + dative-locative -a (back-vowel form, Ming 人名行). dörben is 'four'.

sentences.t: Alčidaj-a qojar miṅγad irge ögbe.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to (written Alčidaj-a with a glide j)
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]

sentences.l: Alčidai-to two thousands people gave.
sentences.i: To Alchidai he gave two thousand people.
sentences.n: Alčidaj-a is Alčidai + dative-locative -a with the glide j. qojar 'two' stands before miṅγad here, so the number stands before the thing counted, as in every gift of this series.

sentences.t: Belgütei-(j)e nigen miṅγan tabun žaγ̇ud irge ögbe.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to (the j is Shiratori’s bracketed glide)
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]

sentences.l: Belgütei-to one thousand five hundreds people gave.
sentences.i: To Belgütei he gave one thousand five hundred people.
sentences.n: Belgütei-(j)e keeps Shiratori's bracketed (j), the glide he writes before the dative -e. The number is built nigen miṅγan tabun žaγ̇ud 'one thousand, five hundreds' (žaγ̇ud is 'hundred' + plural -d, Ming 百每). The ögbe ending 'gave' is the last of the seven gifts.

sentences.t: Daγ̇aritai Kereid-lüġe bolulčaba keġen

morph.gloss: the Kereid, a people [種(名) 一同]
to act together, join in (Ming 共做) [共做了]

sentences.l: Daγ̇aritai Kereid-with acted-together, saying
sentences.i: Saying that Da'aritai had joined with the Kereid,
sentences.n: Kereid-lüġe is the people-name Kereid + comitative -lüġe 'with' (Ming 一同), and bolulčaba is bol- 'be, do' with the 'together' suffix -ulča-, in the past (Ming 共做了 'did together'; the lemma follows the glossary). keġen 'saying' closes it. Shiratori marks nothing, and the subject of 'saying' is not stated; the reply of the three in the following units shows that the speaker is Chinggis, so `i` renders it as indirect speech, with no mark.

sentences.t: nidün-ü ečine ečidgeje keġebešü Boγ̇orču, Muqali Šigi-Qutuqu γurban ügülerün:

morph.gloss: to destroy, do away with (stem inferred from the Ming 滅) [滅咱]
conditional: when (one) has …ed (Ming 呵; ending uncertain)

sentences.l: Eye-of behind let-us-destroy, saying-when, Boγ̇orču, Muqali, Šigi-Qutuqu three saying:
sentences.i: And when he said, “Let us do away with him behind his back,” Bo'orchu, Muqali and Shigi-Qutuqu, the three, said:
sentences.n: nidün-ü ečine is 'behind the eye', Ming 眼的背處 — I take it as 'out of his sight, behind his back'. ečidgeje has a stem ečidge- inferred from the Ming 滅 'destroy' and the first-person hortative -je 'let us'; keġebešü is keġe- 'say' with a conditional ending I cannot analyse closely (Ming 說呵 'when said', so -bešü). The three names are followed by γurban 'three' and ügülerün 'saying'. The speech is not marked off by Shiratori; `i` supplies the marks for the hortative. Doubtful: who is to be destroyed. The reply, 'how can you cast him aside?', shows that it is the uncle Da'aritai.

sentences.t: "Öġer-ün γal(i)-jan sünöġekü metü öġer-ün ger(i)-jen ebdekü metü

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant)
Shiratori’s linking vowel before the reflexive-possessive
to put out, extinguish (stem inferred from the Ming 滅) [滅的]
genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant)
Shiratori’s linking vowel before the reflexive-possessive
to break up, wreck (stem inferred from the Ming 壞) [壞的]

sentences.l: "Own fire putting-out like, own house wrecking like,
sentences.i: “Like putting out one's own fire, like wrecking one's own home,
sentences.n: Two similes, each a participle in -kü plus metü 'like' (Ming 般): sünöġekü and ebdekü, stems inferred from the Ming 滅 and 壞. The possessives γal(i)-jan and ger(i)-jen are the reflexive 'one's own' (-jan after the back-vowel γal, -jen after ger), written with Shiratori's bracketed linking vowel (i). öġer-ün 'of self' repeated before each: 'one's own fire'. Opening mark is Shiratori's on Öġer-ün; the speech runs to atuγai" in a later unit.

sentences.t: sain ečige-jin čin-u geriġes γaγča abaγa čin-u qočorču amu.

morph.gloss: you (stem čin- before the genitive) [你的]
keepsake, token to remember by (the glossary’s gerije; Ming here 道念) [道念]
you (stem čin- before the genitive) [你的]
to lag behind, be left behind [落後着]

sentences.l: Good father-of your keepsakes only uncle your left-behind is.
sentences.i: Of your good father's keepsakes there is only your uncle left.
sentences.n: geriġes is gerije 'keepsake, token to remember by' (the Ming here has 道念; the glossary's gerije has 遺念 elsewhere) + plural -s, 'keepsakes'; čin-u is 'your', the genitive of či on its oblique stem. γaγča 'only, sole' (Ming 獨) and abaγa 'uncle' (Ming 叔). qočorču is a converb 'lagging behind, left behind' and amu 'is': 'is left behind'.

sentences.t: Ker tebčikü.
sentences.l: How cast-aside?
sentences.i: How can he be cast aside?
sentences.n: A short rhetorical question: Ker 'how' (Ming 怎) and tebčikü, a participle in -kü of tebči- 'cast aside' (Ming 棄捨的), 'one to be cast aside'. The subject, the uncle, is understood from the unit before.

sentences.t: In-ü ese uqaγsan-dur bütügei.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

words.reading: 兀中合黑三-突︀舌兒 uqaγsan-dur

morph.gloss: to understand, perceive (stem inferred from the Ming 省) [省的行]
let it not be, do not (prohibitive) [休也者︀]

sentences.l: His not understood-at let-it-not-be.
sentences.i: Do not hold it against him that he did not understand.
sentences.n: In-ü is 'his', the third-person genitive. uqaγsan-dur is the past participle uqaγsan with the dative-locative -dur (Ming 省的行), 'at his having understood', here negated by ese 'not'; the stem uqa- is inferred from the Ming 省 'understand'. bütügei is 'let it not be', a prohibition (Ming 休). 'Hold it against him' is my supplied sense, not in the Mongol: the plain reading is 'let [it] not be, for his not understanding'.

sentences.t: Sain ečige-jin čin-u nilqa nutuγ hüni butaraγ̇ulčažu atuγai"

morph.gloss: you (stem čin- before the genitive) [你的]
young, small, the youngest (Ming 最少) [最小]

words.reading: 不塔舌剌兀勒察周 butaraγ̇ulčažu

morph.gloss: to come out, issue forth (stem inferred from the Ming 出) [共出着]
optative (third person): let it be, let them …

sentences.l: Good father-of your youngest camp smoke making-rise-together let-it-stay"
sentences.i: Let the camp of your good father's youngest stay, sending up its smoke together.”
sentences.n: nutuγ is the 'camp, pasture' and hüni 'smoke' (Ming 煙); butaraγ̇ulčažu is a causative converb with a stem butara- inferred from the Ming 出 'come out' and the 'together' marker -ča- (Ming 共), 'making to come out together'. atuγai (a- 'stay' + -tuγai) is the third-person optative 'let it stay'. nilqa 'youngest' is used without a noun, and I take it as the youngest [of the brothers], that is Da'aritai; this is not stated. Doubtful: 'sending up its smoke together' is the Ming's literal 共出着 with hüni as the object of the causative; as an image for two households sharing a camp it is my reading. The closing quotation mark on atuγai" is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: keġegdežü Qabar-ača hüni qaṅšiala qaγas kelelegdežü že-deli keġen

morph.gloss: nose (the Ming gives 鼻 in brackets; uncertain) [(鼻)行]
to snatch, rush at (stem inferred from the Ming 搶; uncertain) [搶直到]
ending of limit, like -tala: right up to (Ming 直到; uncertain)
separating, clear (Ming 分明; reading uncertain) [分明]
particle: so, very well (Ming 應許 “assent”) [應許罷]
ending of assent: let it be so (Ming 罷; uncertain)

sentences.l: Being-told, nose-from smoke snatching-up-to clearly being-spoken-to, že-deli saying
sentences.i: Being told this plainly, he said, “So be it,”
sentences.n: keġegdežü and kelelegdežü are two passive converbs, 'being told' and 'being spoken to' (-gde- is the passive; Ming 被說着 each time). že-deli (Ming 應許罷) is a word of assent, 'so be it'; keġen 'saying' closes it. Shiratori prints no quotation marks here; the marks round “So be it,” are supplied in `i` only. Doubtful: Qabar-ača hüni qaṅšiala has the Ming 鼻 行 煙 搶直到, 'from the nose, smoke, snatching right up to'; I cannot make an idiom out of it and have left it out of `i`, keeping it in the literal line. qaγas is 'clearly' on the strength of the Ming 分明, a reading the glossary also marks uncertain.

sentences.t: sain ečige-ji sedkižü Boγ̇orču, Muqali, Šigi-Qutuqu γurban-u kelen-dür amurliba-že.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to be at rest, be calmed (Ming 息) [息了也者︀]

sentences.l: Good father-(object) thinking, Boγ̇orču, Muqali, Šigi-Qutuqu three-of word-in was-calmed.
sentences.i: Thinking of his good father, he was calmed by the words of the three, Bo'orchu, Muqali and Shigi-Qutuqu.
sentences.n: ečige-ji is 'the father' with accusative -ji (Ming 父 行), the object of sedkižü 'thinking'. γurban-u is 'of the three' and kelen-dür 'in the word(s)' (dative-locative, Ming 裏); the two together are 'at the words of the three'. amurliba-že is amurli- 'be at rest' (Ming 息) in the past, closed with -že. The subject of amurliba-že is not named; Chinggis is understood, and 'his' good father is supplied in `i`.

sentences.t: Bi eke-de Ödčigin-a tümen irge ögčü nojad-ača Küčü, Kököčü, Žuṅsai, Qorγasun dörben-i tüšibe.

morph.gloss: people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]
to entrust, assign (Ming 委付) [委付了]

sentences.l: I, mother-to Ödčigin-to ten-thousand people giving, officers-from Küčü, Kököčü, Žuṅsai, Qorγasun four-(object) entrusted.
sentences.i: “I have given ten thousand people to Mother and to Ödchigin, and from among the officers I have appointed four to them: Küchü, Kököchü, Jungsai and Qorqasun.
sentences.n: Bi is the first-person pronoun, 'I'; ögčü 'giving' is a converb and tüšibe the past of tüši- 'entrust' (Ming 委付), so the sentence is one converb chain with two datives (eke-de, Ödčigin-a) and an ablative (nojad-ača, 'from the officers', Ming 行). The four names stand in a list before dörben-i 'the four' (accusative). Shiratori marks no speech here, but the next line says basa 'again' Chinggis spoke, which makes this a continuation of his speech; `i` therefore supplies an opening mark here and closes it after Cha'adai's three. The sense of 'to them' (the stewards go with Mother and Ödchigin) is the natural one and not stated.

sentences.t: Žüči-de Qunan, Müṅkegür, Kete γurban-i tüšibe.

morph.gloss: Jüchi, a man’s name [人名 行]
Kete, a man’s name (not the common noun kete “fire-steel”) [人名]
to entrust, assign (Ming 委付) [委付了]

sentences.l: Žüči-to Qunan, Müṅkegür, Kete three-(object) entrusted.
sentences.i: To Jüchi I assigned the three: Qunan, Müngkegür and Kete.
sentences.n: Žüči-de 'to Jüchi'; γurban-i 'the three' (accusative -i, Ming 行); tüšibe 'entrusted'. Kete is a man's name here (Ming 人名), not the common noun kete 'fire-steel' that the glossary has from elsewhere. Müṅke is spelled with a dotted ṅ, which I write ng.

sentences.t: Čaγ̇adai-dur Qaračar, Müṅke, Iduqudai γurban-i tüšibe.

morph.gloss: Cha’adai, a man’s name [人名 行]
to entrust, assign (Ming 委付) [委付了]

sentences.l: Čaγ̇adai-to Qaračar, Müṅke, Iduqudai three-(object) entrusted.
sentences.i: To Cha'adai I assigned the three: Qarachar, Müngke and Iduqudai.”
sentences.n: The same frame again. Čaγ̇adai-dur has dative-locative -dur (after i). Iduqudai is a man's name in the Ming (人名); I keep Shiratori's spelling. The closing quotation mark is supplied by me, to end the speech opened at Bi.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Basa 'again' (Ming 再). Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün: 'Chinggis Qahan, when saying' — the converb -rün that Shiratori uses as an ordinary 'said', with the colon leading into the speech.

sentences.t: "Čaγ̇adai kečeġü bijü. Narin aburitu bijü.
sentences.l: "Čaγ̇adai firm is. Fine-tempered is.
sentences.i: “Cha'adai is firm. He has a fine, subtle temper.
sentences.n: kečeġü (Ming 剛 'hard, firm') and narin aburitu (Ming 細 德性有的, 'fine, having a disposition'): aburi is 'temper, disposition' with the possessive -tu, 'having a (fine) temper'. bijü is bü- 'be' in the present. Doubtful: how narin 'fine' is meant. The Ming gives only the sense 'delicate', and `i` keeps the plain 'fine, subtle'; 'precise' or 'touchy' would be natural readings. Opening quotation mark is Shiratori's on Čaγ̇adai.

sentences.t: Kökesös üde manaγar dergede ažu sedkigsen(i)-jen kelelen atuγai"

morph.gloss: Kökösös, a man’s name (printed Kökesös) [人名]
next morning, early morning (Ming 早) [早]
near, beside (Ming 根前; stem uncertain) [根前]
to think [想了的 自的行]
Shiratori’s linking vowel before the reflexive-possessive
optative (third person): let it be, let them …

sentences.l: Kökesös evening, early near staying, thought-own speaking let-be"
sentences.i: Let Kökösös, staying near, keep saying what he thinks, evening and morning.”
sentences.n: Kökesös is printed so here, against Kökösös earlier (§§208, 223); I write it as the same man in `i`. üde manaγar are 'evening, [and] early morning' (Ming 晩 早), dergede 'near, beside' (Ming 根前), ažu 'staying' (a- + -žu). sedkigsen(i)-jen is sedki- 'think' + the past participle -gsen + Shiratori's bracketed (i) + reflexive -jen, 'what he himself has thought'. kelelen 'speaking' + atuγai 'let it be' is an optative chain: 'let him keep on speaking'. Whom Kökösös is to stay beside is not said in this unit; I take it to be Cha'adai, the man just described. Closing quotation mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.

morph.gloss: to become; with žarliγ, “to make (a decree)” [做了]

sentences.l: Saying, decree made.
sentences.i: So he issued a decree.
sentences.n: keġen 'saying' closes the quotation, and žarliγ bolba is 'made a decree', the same idiom as at the start of §242 (bolžu there, bolba here).

sentences.t: Ögödei-dür Ilüge, Degei qojar-i tüšibe.

morph.gloss: to entrust, assign (Ming 委付) [委付了]

sentences.l: Ögödei-to Ilüge, Degei two-(object) entrusted.
sentences.i: To Ögödei he assigned the two, Ilüge and Degei.
sentences.n: qojar-i 'the two' (qojar + accusative -i, Ming 兩箇) after the two names; Ögödei-dür 'to Ögödei'. In the narrative again, so third person: tüšibe 'entrusted' with no 'I'.

sentences.t: Tolui-dur Čedei, Bala qojar-i tüšibe.

morph.gloss: to entrust, assign (Ming 委付) [委付了]

sentences.l: Tolui-to Čedei, Bala two-(object) entrusted.
sentences.i: To Tolui he assigned the two, Chedei and Bala.
sentences.n: Same frame: Tolui-dur, the two names, qojar-i, tüšibe. Both names are Ming 人名.

sentences.t: Qasar-tur Žebke-ji tüšibe.

words.reading: 中合撒舌兒-突︀舌兒 Qasar-tur

morph.gloss: Qasar, a man’s name [人名 行]
dative-locative: to, with (back-vowel form, after r)
Jebke, a man’s name [人名 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to entrust, assign (Ming 委付) [委付了]

sentences.l: Qasar-to Žebke-(object) entrusted.
sentences.i: To Qasar he assigned Jebke.
sentences.n: Qasar-tur is 'to Qasar' (dative-locative -tur after r); Žebke-ji is the name + accusative -ji (after a vowel). A Jebke of the Jalairtai is named again at the end of §244; presumably the same man, but the text does not say so.

sentences.t: Alčidai-dur Čaγ̇urγai-ji tüšibe.

morph.gloss: Alchidai, a man’s name [人名 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to entrust, assign (Ming 委付) [委付了]

sentences.l: Alčidai-to Čaγ̇urγai-(object) entrusted.
sentences.i: To Alchidai he assigned Cha'urqai.
sentences.n: Alčidai-dur 'to Alchidai'; Čaγ̇urγai-ji is the name + accusative -ji. Čaγ̇urγai is Ming 人名; I write Cha'urqai (γ̇ → ', γ → q).

sentences.t: Qoṅγotadai Müṅlig ečiġe-jin köġüd doloγ̇an büleġei.

morph.gloss: past: used to be, there was (Ming 來)

sentences.l: Qoṅγotadai Müṅlig father-of sons seven there-were.
sentences.i: Father Münlig of the Qongqotadai had seven sons.
sentences.n: Qoṅγotadai is a people (Ming 種(名)); Müṅlig ečiġe-jin köġüd is 'Münlig father-of sons' — ečiġe-jin 'of the father' (genitive -jin after a vowel) is the usual 'Father Münlig', and köġüd is köġün 'son' + plural -d. doloγ̇an 'seven'. büleġei is bü- 'be' + -leġei, a past 'there were, used to be' (Ming 有來).

sentences.t: Doloγ̇an-u dundatu Kököčü Teb-Teṅgeri büleġe.

morph.gloss: past: used to be, there was (Ming 來)

sentences.l: Seven-of middle Kököčü Teb-Teṅgeri there-was.
sentences.i: Of the seven, the middle one was Kököchü, called Teb-Tenggeri.
sentences.n: Doloγ̇an-u is 'of the seven' and dundatu 'the middle one' (dunda 'middle' + possessive -tu, Ming 中間). Teb-Teṅgeri is a shaman's name (Ming 巫名). Doubtful: whether it is a second name or a title (Kököchü 'called' Teb-Tenggeri); the Ming gives only 'a shaman's name'. büleġe is the same past 'was' as in the last unit, singular now.

sentences.t: Tede doloγ̇an Qoṅγotan Qasar-i ömerežu žančižuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: Qasar, a man’s name [(人)名 行]
to band together, take sides (stem inferred from the Ming 黨比) [黨比着]
to strike, beat (stem inferred from the Ming 打) [打了來]

sentences.l: Those seven Qoṅγotan Qasar-(object) banding-together struck.
sentences.i: Those seven Qongqotan ganged up on Qasar and beat him.
sentences.n: Tede 'those' (plural of tere), doloγ̇an 'seven', Qoṅγotan a clan (Ming 種(名)); Qasar-i is the object. ömerežu is a converb of ömere-, a stem inferred from the Ming 黨比着 'sticking together in a clique, taking sides'; žančižuγ̇ui is the past narrative of žanči- 'strike' (Ming 打了來, stem inferred). So 'ganging up' is the Ming's sense, not a recorded meaning of ömere-.

sentences.t: Qasar doloγ̇an Qoṅγotan-a ömerežu žančiγdaγ̇a keġen Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a šögödüġešü

morph.gloss: dative-locative: by (agent of a passive; Ming 行)
to band together, take sides (stem inferred from the Ming 黨比) [黨着]
to strike, beat (stem inferred from the Ming 打) [被打了]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
to kneel and report (stem inferred from the Ming 跪吿) [跪吿呵]
conditional: if, when (printed with š; Ming 呵)

sentences.l: Qasar seven Qoṅγotan-by banding-together was-beaten, saying Chinggis Qaγan-to kneeling-reporting-if
sentences.i: When it was told on bended knee to Chinggis Qahan that Qasar had been beaten by the seven Qongqotan ganging up on him,
sentences.n: žančiγdaγ̇a is žanči- 'strike' + the passive -γda- + a past ending (Ming 被打了 'was beaten'); the agent Qoṅγotan-a takes the dative-locative -a (Ming 行), a pattern the glossary notes with passives. keġen 'saying' closes the report, and šögödüġešü is a conditional/time converb of šögödü- (stem inferred from the Ming 跪吿呵 'kneeling and telling') — 'when [one] knelt and told'. Doubtful: who is the teller. Qasar is named in the third person, so he is not the speaker; `i` leaves it unstated. Shiratori marks no speech.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan busud-tur kiliṅlažu aqui dunda kelelekü bolun

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
dative-locative: at, to (back-vowel form, after d)
to be angry (stem inferred from the Ming 怒) [怒着]
middle, in the middle of [中間]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan others-at being-angry, being, in-the-midst speaking becoming
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, angry at the others and in the midst of speaking,
sentences.n: busud-tur is busu 'other' + plural -d + dative-locative -tur, 'at the others' (Ming 別的每 行); kiliṅlažu 'being angry' (stem inferred from the Ming 怒) and aqui, the participle of a- 'be' (Ming 有), run together, 'angry, being'. dunda is 'in the middle' (Ming 中間) and kelelekü bolun 'speaking, becoming' (kelelekü a participle, bolun the converb of bol-; Ming 說的 做): I read 'in the midst of speaking', with Chinggis as the speaker, as the next unit shows. Doubtful: who the 'others' are: the Ming does not say whether other people present or the Qongqotan; the plain reading is that the Qahan's anger was already turned elsewhere.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan kilin-dur(i)-jan Qasar-i ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Shiratori’s linking vowel before the reflexive-possessive
Qasar, a man’s name [人名 行]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan anger-in-own Qasar-(object) saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, in his own anger, said to Qasar:
sentences.n: kilin-dur(i)-jan is kilin 'anger' (Ming 怒) + dative-locative -dur + Shiratori's bracketed (i) + reflexive -jan, 'in his own anger'. Qasar-i carries the accusative -i (Ming 行) for the person addressed. ügülerün 'saying' leads into the speech. The anger shifts on to Qasar here, as the next two units show.

sentences.t: "Amitu-da ülü ilaγdaqu-ača büleġe či.

words.reading: 亦剌黑荅中忽-阿察 ilaγdaqu-ača

morph.gloss: to overcome, defeat (stem inferred from the Ming 勝; the glossary’s stem, compare ilaγdaqu) [被勝了有 行]
past: used to be, there was (Ming 來)

sentences.l: "Living-among not being-defeated-from there-were you.
sentences.i: “You were one who was not to be beaten by the living.
sentences.n: Amitu-da is amitu 'living' (amin 'life' + possessive -tu) + dative-locative -da (Ming 性命有的 行), which with a passive can mark the agent, 'by the living'. ilaγdaqu-ača is ilaγ- 'overcome' (stem inferred from the Ming 勝; the glossary's stem) + the passive -da- + participle -qu + ablative -ača, and ülü 'not' before it: 'from not being overcome'. büleġe či is 'you were'. Doubtful: the ablative after a participle is an odd form; the Ming 被勝了有 行 only shows it is a passive of 'beat', and the sense 'you were not to be beaten by anyone alive' is my reading. Opening quotation mark is Shiratori's on Amitu-da.

sentences.t: Ker ilaγdaγ̇a či"

morph.gloss: to overcome, defeat (stem inferred from the Ming 勝; the glossary’s stem, compare ilaγdaqu) [被勝了]

sentences.l: How were-beaten you?"
sentences.i: How were you beaten?”
sentences.n: Ker 'how' (Ming 怎生), ilaγdaγ̇a 'was beaten' (ilaγ- + passive -da- + a past ending; Ming 被勝了), či 'you'. The closing quotation mark on či" is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: keġegdežü Qasar nilbusu aldaγ̇ad bosču jorčižu

morph.gloss: to let fall, drop (Ming 墮) [墮了]
converb of completed action: having …ed (back-vowel form)

sentences.l: Being-told, Qasar tears letting-fall, rising, going-off,
sentences.i: Told this, Qasar let his tears fall, got up and went off,
sentences.n: keġegdežü 'being told' (passive converb) leads in; nilbusu aldaγ̇ad is 'tears having dropped' — alda- 'let fall, drop' (Ming 墮了) is the verb, aldaγ̇ad a converb of completed action; bosču 'rising' and jorčižu 'going' are two more converbs. All four converbs wait for the finite verb in the next unit.

sentences.t: Qasar maγ̇uilažu γurban üdür ese irebe.

morph.gloss: verb-maker: to act as, to be …

sentences.l: Qasar being-vexed three day not came.
sentences.i: Qasar, vexed, did not come for three days.
sentences.n: maγ̇uilažu is maγ̇ui 'bad' + verb-maker -la- + converb -žu (Ming 煩惱着 'being troubled'), 'taking it badly'. γurban üdür is 'three days', ese irebe 'did not come' (ese + past of ire-). The finite verb, at last, of the chain begun two units back.

sentences.t: Tende Teb-Teṅgeri Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Then Teb-Teṅgeri Chinggis Qaγan-to saying:
sentences.i: Then Teb-Tenggeri said to Chinggis Qahan:
sentences.n: Tende 'there, then' (Ming 那裏). Qaγ̇an-a is 'to the qahan' with the dative-locative -a (Ming 行), as in Qasar-a above. ügülerün 'saying' leads into the speech, which opens at Müṅke in the next unit.

sentences.t: "Müṅke teṅgeri-jin žarliγ qān žaγ̇arid ügülemü.

morph.gloss: Heaven, the sky as a power [天的]
qan, ruler (short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]
revelation, divine sign (Ming 神吿) [神︀吿每]

sentences.l: "Eternal Heaven-of decree, qan, signs speak.
sentences.i: “The decree of Eternal Heaven, the Qan: the signs say it.
sentences.n: Müṅke 'eternal' (Ming 長生 'long life') teṅgeri-jin 'of Heaven' (genitive -jin after a vowel): 'Eternal Heaven's decree' (žarliγ, Ming 聖旨). žaγ̇arid is the plural (-d) of žaγ̇arin, 'signs, revelations' (Ming 神吿 each), ügülemü the present 'speaks' (-mü). Doubtful: qān stands bare between the decree and the signs (Ming 皇帝) and I cannot tell its function — an address, an apposition, or the object of what the signs say; `i` leaves it as a bare word. Opening quotation mark is Shiratori's on Müṅke.

sentences.t: Nigente Temüžin ulus barituγai keġemü.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: “one time, once” (Ming 一次; uncertain)
to take hold of, seize [把者︀]
optative (third person): let it be, let them …

sentences.l: Once Temüžin realm let-him-hold, says.
sentences.i: Once it says, ‘Let Temüjin hold the realm.’
sentences.n: Nigente is nigen 'one' + dative-locative -te, 'at one time' (the Ming 一次, 'one occasion'), repeated in the next line, so 'once … another time'. barituγai is bari- 'hold, seize' + the optative -tuγai ('let him …'), and keġemü 'says' (keġe- + present -mü) closes it as a quotation. The inner marks are mine: Shiratori prints none, but keġemü shows a quoted wish.

sentences.t: Nigente Qasar-i keġemü.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: “one time, once” (Ming 一次; uncertain)
Qasar, a man’s name [(人)名 行]

sentences.l: Once Qasar-(object) says.
sentences.i: Another time it names Qasar.
sentences.n: Nigente 'at one time' again, Qasar-i with the accusative, keġemü 'says'. The verb of the first line is understood: what the signs say about Qasar is left unspoken here, and `i` renders keġemü as 'names'. Doubtful: the Ming gives no more than 一次行 說有 'on another occasion says'.

sentences.t: Qasar-i ese nemdeġešü medeġe ügei bi-že"

morph.gloss: Qasar, a man’s name [(人)名 行]
to forestall, cut in first (stem inferred from the Ming 掩襲) [掩襲呵]
conditional: if, when (printed with š; Ming 呵)

sentences.l: Qasar-(object) not forestalling-if knowing without is"
sentences.i: If Qasar is not forestalled, there is no knowing what will come.”
sentences.n: nemdeġešü is the conditional of nemde- 'forestall, strike first' (stem inferred from the Ming 掩襲, 'attack by surprise'), with ese 'not' before it: 'if one does not forestall'. medeġe ügei is 'knowing — without', Ming 知 無, and bi-že 'is indeed' closes it. The closing quotation mark on bi-že" is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: keġegdežü Čiṅgis Qaγan mün süni morilažu Qasar-i barira oduγ̇asu

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
just, the very (particle; Ming 只) [只]
verb-maker: to act as, to be …
converb of purpose: in order to … (uncertain)
to go (stem inferred from the Ming 去) [去呵]
conditional: if, when (back-vowel form; Ming 呵)

sentences.l: Being-told, Chinggis Qaγan that night mounting, Qasar-(object) to-seize going-when,
sentences.i: Told this, Chinggis Qahan mounted his horse that same night, and when he set out to seize Qasar,
sentences.n: morilažu is morin 'horse' + verb-maker -la- + -žu (Ming 上馬着 'mounting'). barira is bari- 'seize' with a purpose-converb ending -ra (Ming 拿 'to seize'; the ending is my reading); oduγ̇asu is od- 'go' (stem inferred from the Ming 去) with the conditional -uγ̇asu, 'when he went'. mün (Ming 只) is 'just, that very'. The clause is incomplete here: the main verb comes after the Küchü and Kököchü clause.

sentences.t: Küčü, Kököčü qojar Qasar-i barira odba keġen eke-de žaγ̇ažiγ̇u.

morph.gloss: converb of purpose: in order to … (uncertain)
to tell, report (stem inferred from the Ming 吿) [吿了有]

sentences.l: Küčü, Kököčü two Qasar-(object) to-seize went, saying, mother-to told.
sentences.i: Küchü and Kököchü, the two, told Mother, saying, “He has gone to seize Qasar.”
sentences.n: qojar 'two' follows the pair it counts. barira odba keġen is 'went to seize, saying', the quoted words closed by keġen; žaγ̇ažiγ̇u is the past of žaγ̇a- 'tell, report' (stem and ending inferred from the Ming 吿了有). Doubtful: who 'went'. The Ming reads 人名 人名 兩箇 人名 拿 去了 麽道 with no subject marked for odba. I take it as Chinggis ('he has gone') because Küchü and Kököchü are Mother's stewards (§243) and report to her; read the other way, the two would have gone themselves. The quotation marks are supplied in `i`.

sentences.t: eke medeġed süni böġed udaγ̇aran Čaγaγ̇an temeġen kölžü qaraγ̇utai tergetei

morph.gloss: converb of completed action: having …ed (front-vowel form)
right after, straightway (Ming 隨卽; analysis uncertain) [隨卽]
to yoke, harness (stem inferred from the Ming 駕) [駕着]

sentences.l: Mother knowing, night indeed straightway white camel harnessing, black-having cart-having
sentences.i: Mother, on learning of it, harnessed a white camel that same night to her black cart,
sentences.n: Eke medeġed 'Mother, having known' (medeġed, a converb in -ġed). böġed (Ming 便) and udaγ̇aran (Ming 隨卽) both mean 'at once, then'; the second I cannot analyse. kölžü is köl- 'yoke' (stem inferred from the Ming 駕着 'harnessing'). qaraγ̇utai tergetei is 'black — cart-having' (Ming 黑 車有的). Doubtful: whether 'black' goes with the cart or the camel, and what -γ̇utai is; I put it on the cart.

sentences.t: süni-de dülin jorčižu naran urγuqui-luγ̇a kürüġesü

morph.gloss: to press on without halting (stem inferred from the Ming 兼行) [兼行]

words.reading: 兀舌兒中忽中灰-魯阿 urγuqui-luγ̇a

morph.gloss: to rise, come up (stem inferred from the Ming 出) [纔出呵]
conditional: if, when (front-vowel form; Ming 呵)

sentences.l: Night-in pressing-on going, sun rising-with arriving-when
sentences.i: and pressed on through the night, and when she reached the place as the sun was rising,
sentences.n: süni-de is 'by night' (dative-locative -de, Ming 夜行); dülin is a converb of düli- 'press on without halting' (Ming 兼行, stem inferred); jorčižu 'going'. urγuqui-luγ̇a is urγu- 'rise' (stem inferred from the Ming 出, 'come out') + the participle -qui + comitative -luγ̇a (Ming 纔出呵), 'with the rising [of the sun]'; kürüġesü 'on arriving'. 'The place' is supplied: the verb has no object.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Qasar-un qančud hujažu maqalai büse in-ü abču

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
sleeve (Ming 衣袖; stem inferred) [衣袖(每)]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan Qasar-of sleeves tying, cap, belt his taking
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan had tied Qasar's sleeves and, taking his cap and belt,
sentences.n: hujažu is huja- 'knot, bind' (Ming 拴着) + converb -žu; qančud 'sleeves' (Ming 衣袖) is a plural form with a stem I infer. So the Qahan has bound Qasar by tying his sleeves, and taken his cap and belt. The subject of the converbs is Chinggis, as the Mongol has it; Mother's arrival has just been told and is told again two units on, so `i` adds no 'she found'. in-ü 'his' is Qasar's.

sentences.t: üge in-ü asaγun büküi-dür

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Words his asking being-at
sentences.i: was asking him for his account,
sentences.n: üge in-ü asaγun is 'word his asking' (asaγ- 'ask' + converb -un), and büküi-dür 'in the being' (the participle -küi + dative-locative -dür, Ming 有 時) makes it 'at the time of his asking'. The 'account' is a free rendering of üge 'word, speech'.

sentences.t: eke-de kürtežü Čiṅgis Qaγan gejegčü eke-dēče emiġebe.

morph.gloss: to arrive, come to (from kür-; the Ming 被到着 reads it passive; uncertain) [被到着]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
to be startled, alarmed (stem inferred from the Ming 驚駭) [驚駭着]
ablative: from (front-vowel form; the glossary’s eke-dēče has the Ming 處 “place”, here 行)
to be afraid, in dread (stem inferred from the Ming 惶懼) [惶懼了]

sentences.l: Mother-to being-reached, Chinggis Qaγan startled, mother-from was-afraid.
sentences.i: Mother reached them. Chinggis Qahan was startled, and was afraid of Mother.
sentences.n: eke-de kürtežü is 'being reached by Mother' (the Ming reads 被到着, passive; kürte- is from kür- 'reach'), i.e. 'when Mother came to them'. gejegčü 'startled' and emiġebe 'was afraid' have stems inferred from the Ming 驚駭 and 惶懼. eke-dēče is 'from the mother' with the ablative -dēče (the Ming here writes 母行; the glossary's eke-dēče has 母 處 'place'), the long ē as Shiratori prints it: 'afraid of her', literally 'in dread from her'. Doubtful: the passive reading of kürtežü; the plain active 'arriving' would give the same story.

sentences.t: Eke aγ̇urlažu kürčü tergen-eče baγ̇uγ̇ad

morph.gloss: verb-maker: to act as, to be …
converb of completed action: having …ed (back-vowel form)

sentences.l: Mother being-angry arriving, cart-from descended,
sentences.i: Mother, angry, arrived, came down from her cart,
sentences.n: aγ̇urlažu is aγ̇ur 'breath, rage' + -la- + -žu, 'raging'; kürčü 'arriving' (kür- 'reach' + -čü); tergen-eče is 'from the cart' (ablative -eče); baγ̇uγ̇ad is baγ̇u- 'come down' + the converb of completed action -γ̇ad. The chain of converbs runs on through the next units and ends only in ügülerün.

sentences.t: eke öġesün Qasar-un hujaγsad qančud daižu talbiγ̇ad

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
to knot, bind (Ming 拴) [拴了的(每)]
past participle, plural: those who have …ed (Ming 每)
sleeve (Ming 衣袖; stem inferred) [袖每]
to untie, loosen (stem inferred from the Ming 解) [解着]
to let go, release (Ming 放) [放了]
converb of completed action: having …ed (back-vowel form)

sentences.l: Mother herself Qasar-of tied-ones sleeves untying, letting-go,
sentences.i: and herself untied the knotted sleeves of Qasar, and let them go,
sentences.n: öġesün 'herself' is the emphatic pronoun (Ming 自己); hujaγsad is the plural participle of huja- 'tie' (Ming 拴了的每), 'the tied ones', qualifying qančud 'sleeves'. daižu 'untying' (stem inferred from the Ming 解着) and talbiγ̇ad 'letting go' (Ming 放了). öġesün is rendered 'herself'.

sentences.t: maqalai büse in-ü Qasar-a ögčü

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
Qasar, a man’s name [人名 行]

sentences.l: Cap, belt his Qasar-to giving
sentences.i: and gave Qasar back his cap and belt.
sentences.n: maqalai büse in-ü is 'cap, belt, his'; Qasar-a 'to Qasar'; ögčü 'giving' (ög- + -čü). 'Back' is supplied: the Mongol has only 'giving', but the objects are the ones taken in the unit before.

sentences.t: eke kiliṅlažu aγ̇ur(i)-jan darun jadan žabilan saγ̇užu

morph.gloss: to be angry (stem inferred from the Ming 怒) [怒着]
Shiratori’s linking vowel before the reflexive-possessive

sentences.l: Mother being-angry, own rage pressing unable, cross-legged sitting
sentences.i: Mother, in her anger unable to hold down her rage, sat down cross-legged,
sentences.n: aγ̇ur(i)-jan is aγ̇ur 'rage' + Shiratori's (i) + reflexive -jan, 'her own rage'; darun jadan is 'pressing down, unable' (daru- 'press', jada- 'be unable', both converbs in -n; Ming 壓 不得). žabilan (Ming 盤) is cross-legged, an adverb whose stem I do not know; saγ̇užu 'sitting'.

sentences.t: qojar kököd(i)-jen γarγažu qojar ebüdüg degeġün bisariγ̇ulžu ügülerün:

morph.gloss: breast (Ming 乳 “milk, breast”) [乳每 自的行]
Shiratori’s linking vowel before the reflexive-possessive
above, upon (Ming 上; the glossary has 從上 “from above” elsewhere) [上]
to be full, overflow (stem inferred from the Ming 盈滿) [盈滿着]

sentences.l: Two breasts-own drawing-out, two knees upon overflowing, saying:
sentences.i: She drew out her two breasts and let them spill over her two knees, and said:
sentences.n: kököd(i)-jen is kökö 'breast' (Ming 乳, 'milk, breast') + plural -d + Shiratori's (i) + reflexive -jen, 'her own breasts'; γarγažu is γar- 'go out' + causative -γa- + -žu, 'making come out, drawing out'. bisariγ̇ulžu (stem bisari-, from the Ming 盈滿 'full to overflowing') + causative: 'letting overflow'; degeġün is 'upon' (Ming 上; the glossary has 從上 elsewhere). Doubtful: the exact picture — the Ming says only 'filled over'; breasts hanging over her crossed knees is the natural reading.

sentences.t: "Üžebe-ü kökögsen kökön tan-u ene bi.

morph.gloss: question particle: is it so? (Ming 麽)
to suckle, give the breast (stem inferred from the Ming 乳) [乳了的]

sentences.l: "Seen? Suckled breast of-you-all this is.
sentences.i: “Have you seen? This is the breast that nursed you.
sentences.n: Üžebe-ü is üže- 'see' + past -be + the question particle -ü (Ming 見了麽). kökögsen is the past participle of a verb kökö- 'to suckle' (inferred from the Ming 乳了的 'suckled'), kökön 'breast, milk'. tan-u is 'your (plural)', ene 'this' (singular, and kökön singular: the breast of which Mother goes on to speak), and bi here is 'is' (Ming 有), not 'I'. Doubtful: the grammar of kökögsen kökön tan-u — 'the nursed breasts, yours' — is clear in sense but not in analysis; the plural 'your' (tan-u) addresses the sons. Opening quotation mark is Shiratori's on Üžebe-ü.

sentences.t: Ede qadalun daγ̇un qarbisu-γ̇an qažaγsad küi-jen tasuluγsad Qasar jakibe.

morph.gloss: to trace to the root, search out (house reading; no Ming gloss here)
sound, voice (house reading; no Ming gloss here)
afterbirth, placenta (Ming 胞衣) [胞衣 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one’s own (the form after a vowel)
to bite, gnaw (Ming 咬) [咬了的(每)]
past participle, plural: those who have …ed (Ming 每)
umbilical cord (Ming 臍帶) [臍帶自的行]
to sever, cut through (Ming 斷) [斷(了)的每]
past participle, plural: those who have …ed (Ming 每)
to do what? (Ming 做甚) [做甚來]

sentences.l: These tracing-to-root voice, afterbirth-own gnawing-ones cord-own severing-ones Qasar what-did.
sentences.i: These—the ones who gnawed their own afterbirth and cut their own cord—what did Qasar do?
sentences.n: Ede qadalun daγ̇un has no Ming gloss at all; I give them the meanings the glossary has for these forms elsewhere ('these', 'tracing to the root', 'voice'), but I do not know what they mean here and `i` carries only Ede. Then two plural participles with the reflexive: qarbisu-γ̇an 'their own afterbirth' (qarbisu with -γ̇an, Ming 胞衣 自), qažaγsad 'those who gnawed' (Ming 咬了的); küi-jen 'their own cord' (Ming 臍帶 自), tasuluγsad 'those who severed' (Ming 斷了的). jakibe is the past of jaki-, 'to do what?' (Ming 做甚來): 'what did Qasar do?'. Doubtful: whether the 'ones who gnawed' are the brothers collectively (my reading) or a general proverbial phrase.

sentences.t: Temüžin ene nigen kökö min-u baraqu büleġe.

morph.gloss: breast (Ming 乳 “milk, breast”; not the colour kökö “blue”) [乳]
my, of me (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
to be finished, used up; here “to finish, drain” (Ming 喫了) [喫了]
past: used to be, there was (Ming 來)

sentences.l: Temüžin this one breast my finishing there-was.
sentences.i: Temüjin used to finish only this one breast of mine.
sentences.n: baraqu is bara- 'be finished, used up' + participle -qu (Ming 喫了 'ate, finished'), with büleġe 'was', which makes the past habitual (compare qaraqu büleġe in §4, 'used to see'): 'used to finish'. kökö 'breast' here (Ming 乳) is not the colour word kökö 'blue' of the glossary. min-u 'of mine' follows its noun. The point of the next lines is a comparison of appetites, and `i` keeps it plain.

sentences.t: Qačiγ̇un, Ödčigin qojaγ̇ula bolžu nigen kökö ülü baraqu büleġe.

morph.gloss: the two together (collective numeral, from qojar) [兩箇]
breast (Ming 乳 “milk, breast”; not the colour kökö “blue”) [乳]
to be finished, used up; here “to finish, drain” (Ming 喫了) [喫了]
past: used to be, there was (Ming 來)

sentences.l: Qačiγ̇un, Ödčigin the-two being one breast not finishing there-was.
sentences.i: Qachi'un and Ödchigin, the two of them together, would not finish even one breast.
sentences.n: qojaγ̇ula is a collective 'the two together' (Ming 兩箇), a form of qojar, and bolžu 'becoming' puts them in one subject. ülü baraqu büleġe is 'not finishing — was', the negative of the unit before. nigen kökö 'one breast', the same as above.

sentences.t: Qasar bürün qojar büri kököd min-u baražu

morph.gloss: my, of me (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
to be finished, used up; here “to finish, drain” [喫了着]

sentences.l: Qasar being, two every breast my finishing
sentences.i: As for Qasar, finishing both my breasts,
sentences.n: bürün is bü- 'be' with the converb -rün (Ming 有), here the topic 'as for'. qojar büri kököd min-u is 'two — every — breast(s) — mine' (büri 'each, every', here Ming 全 'whole'; kököd the plural of kökö). baražu 'finishing' (converb), the same verb as baraqu above.

sentences.t: čeġeži min-u aγ̇ui boltala amurliγ̇ulžu čeġeži aγ̇ui bolγaqu büleġe.

morph.gloss: my, of me (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]

words.reading: 阿木舌兒里兀勒周 amurliγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: to be at rest, be calm [安寗了着]
past: used to be, there was (Ming 來)

sentences.l: Bosom my wide until-becoming calming, bosom wide to-make there-was.
sentences.i: until my bosom was wide, and easing it, he would make my bosom wide.
sentences.n: čeġeži min-u aγ̇ui boltala is 'my bosom, wide, until becoming' (bol- + -tala 'until', Ming 做直到). amurliγ̇ulžu is amurli- 'be at rest' + causative -γ̇ul- + -žu (Ming 安寗了着), 'calming'. bolγaqu is bol- + causative -γa- + -qu, 'to make into', and büleġe 'was', the past habitual: 'used to make [it] wide'. Qasar is the subject throughout: finishing (baražu), easing (amurliγ̇ulžu), he would make it wide. The picture is that the nursing eased her chest — the whole sentence is a mother's account of Qasar as a child.

sentences.t: Teġü-ber erdemtü Temüžin min-u čeġeži erdemtü Qasar min-u qabu küčü erdemtü tula

morph.gloss: that (stem of tere before a case ending) [爲那般]
skill, talent (Ming 技能) [技能 有的]
my, of me (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
skill, talent (Ming 技能) [技能 有的]
my, of me (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
shooting an arrow, archery (Ming 射箭) [射箭]
skill, talent (Ming 技能) [技能 有的]
because of, on account of (postposition) [上頭]

sentences.l: Therefore skilled my-Temüžin bosom skilled, my-Qasar archery strength skilled because,
sentences.i: Therefore, since my Temüjin is gifted in the bosom, and my Qasar gifted in archery and strength,
sentences.n: Teġü-ber is the stem teġü- 'that' + instrumental -ber, 'therefore' (Ming 爲那般). erdemtü is erdem 'skill' + possessive -tü, 'skilled, having skill' (Ming 技能有的). The parallel is Temüžin … čeġeži erdemtü and Qasar … qabu küčü erdemtü, with tula 'because of' (Ming 上頭) governing both. Doubtful: the first erdemtü stands before Temüžin and the second after čeġeži, so the word order is uncertain; min-u follows the name it belongs to (Temüžin min-u 'my Temüjin', Qasar min-u 'my Qasar'), as at the start of §242, and not čeġeži. I read 'gifted [in] the bosom' for Temüjin (his wit, as the contrast with Qasar's archery implies) and 'gifted in archery, strength' for Qasar. A sentence of Mother's praise, not a plain statement.

sentences.t: qarbučažu γaruγsan-i qarbužu oroγ̇ulqu büleġe.

morph.gloss: to go out [出了的 行]
past: used to be, there was (Ming 來)

sentences.l: Shoot-crossing, going-out-ones shooting, to-make-enter there-was.
sentences.i: shooting across, shooting at those who had gone out, he would drive them in.
sentences.n: qarbučažu is qarbu- 'shoot an arrow' (Ming 射箭) + a suffix -ča- I read from the Ming 交參着 'crossing, mixing' + -žu, 'shooting crossways'; qarbužu repeats qarbu- + -žu, so both verbs of shooting stand in `i`. γaruγsan-i is 'the ones who went out' (γar- + the participle -γsan + accusative -i), oroγ̇ulqu is oro- 'enter' + causative -γ̇ul- + -qu, 'to make enter', with büleġe. Doubtful: the sense of 'across' is from the Ming 交參 alone; 'those who had gone out' may be cattle, animals or men, and the unit says no more.

sentences.t: Oγžadču γaruγsan-i hontučažu oroγ̇ulqu büleġe.

morph.gloss: to be startled; here “to startle” (stem inferred from the Ming 驚; the strays are the object) [驚着]
to go out [出了的 行]
to shoot from afar (stem inferred from the Ming 遠箭射) [遠箭射着]
past: used to be, there was (Ming 來)

sentences.l: Startling going-out-ones from-afar shooting to-make-enter there-was.
sentences.i: Startling those who had gone out, he would shoot at them from afar and drive them in.
sentences.n: Oγžadču is a converb of oγžad- (stem inferred from the Ming 驚着; the glossary glosses the same form 'being startled', but here the strays are the object, so 'startling', as the Ming 驚 allows); hontučažu is hontuča- 'shoot from afar' (stem inferred from the Ming 遠箭射着). The rest is the same as the unit before, so the two are one thought: Qasar's gift is in bringing back what has strayed.

sentences.t: Edöġe daisun küġün-i muqudγaba. keġežü Qasar-i üžen jadamui ta" keġebe.

morph.gloss: to wipe out, destroy (stem inferred from the Ming 窮絕) [窮絕了]
Qasar, a man’s name [人名 行]

sentences.l: Now enemy people-(object) destroyed, saying, Qasar-(object) seeing unable you" said.
sentences.i: Now ‘He has wiped out the enemy,’ you say, and you cannot bear to look at Qasar,” she said.
sentences.n: daisun küġün-i is 'enemy people (object)', muqudγaba 'destroyed' (stem muqudγa- inferred from the Ming 窮絕), keġežü 'saying'. Qasar-i üžen jadamui ta is 'Qasar-(object), seeing, is unable, you' (üže- 'see' + -n; jada- 'be unable' + -mui; Ming 見 不得有). The closing quotation mark is Shiratori's on ta", and it closes the speech that opened at Üžebe-ü; keġebe 'said' follows it. The inner marks on 'He has wiped out the enemy' are mine. Doubtful: the clause means either 'now that he has beaten the enemy, you cannot stand to see him' or that Qasar is being called the enemy; I take the first.

sentences.t: Eke-ji amurliγ̇ulun baražu Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to be at rest, be calm [寗息]
to be finished, used up; here “to finish, drain” [了着]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.l: Mother-(object) calming, Chinggis Qaγan saying:
sentences.i: Having soothed Mother, Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Eke-ji is 'Mother' with the accusative -ji (Ming 行), amurliγ̇ulun is a converb of the causative 'to calm' and baražu 'finishing' makes it 'having soothed'. Doubtful: whether the calming is Chinggis's act; the Mongol gives no agent for the converbs, and the structure makes the Qahan the one who soothes before he speaks.

sentences.t: "Eke-ji kiliṅlaγdažu ajun ba ajuba.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to be angry (stem inferred from the Ming 怒) [被怒着]
to fear (stem inferred from the Ming 怕) [怕]
to fear (stem inferred from the Ming 怕) [怕了]

sentences.l: "Mother-by being-angered, fearing also was-afraid.
sentences.i: “Angered by Mother, I was afraid—indeed afraid.
sentences.n: kiliṅlaγdažu is kiliṅla- 'be angry' + passive -γda- + -žu (Ming 被怒着 'being angered'); Eke-ji with the accusative -ji marks the one who angers, 'by Mother' (Ming 行). ajun ba ajuba is 'fearing, also, feared': a verb doubled around ba 'also' for emphasis; the stem aju- is inferred from the Ming 怕. Opening quotation mark is Shiratori's on Eke-ji.

sentences.t: Hičen ba hičebe bi"

morph.gloss: to be ashamed (stem inferred from the Ming 羞) [羞]
to be ashamed (stem inferred from the Ming 羞) [羞了]

sentences.l: Ashamed also was-ashamed I"
sentences.i: Ashamed, indeed ashamed, was I.”
sentences.n: The same doubling as the unit before: Hičen ba hičebe, 'being ashamed — also — was ashamed' (hiče-, stem inferred from the Ming 羞). bi is 'I'. The closing mark is Shiratori's on bi".

sentences.t: keġežü ičuja" bida.

morph.gloss: to withdraw, retreat (stem inferred from the Ming 退) [退咱]

sentences.l: Saying, let-us-withdraw" we.
sentences.i: Saying, “Let us withdraw, you and I,”
sentences.n: ičuja is ič- 'withdraw' (stem inferred from the Ming 退) with the first-person hortative -ja after a linking vowel -u- (uncertain); bida is 'we', inclusive (Ming 咱 'you and I'), which I render 'you and I'. Doubtful: Shiratori prints a closing mark at ičuja" with no opening mark for it; `i` supplies the opening mark and puts the closing mark after bida, taking the pronoun into the quoted words, though Shiratori prints it before bida. Whom Chinggis addresses is not stated.

sentences.t: keġežü ičuba.

morph.gloss: to withdraw, retreat (stem inferred from the Ming 退) [退了]

sentences.l: Saying, withdrew.
sentences.i: he withdrew.
sentences.n: keġežü 'saying' and ičuba, the past of ič- with the same linking -u-. Chinggis withdraws and does nothing more to Qasar in front of Mother.

sentences.t: Eke-de ülü medeġülün ečineġün Qasar-un irge in-ü abču

morph.gloss: secretly, behind (someone’s back) (Ming 暗地; related to ečine “behind”; ending uncertain) [暗地行]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Mother-to not informing, secretly Qasar-of people his taking
sentences.i: Without letting Mother know, in secret, he took Qasar's people from him
sentences.n: ülü medeġülün is 'not — making known' (mede- 'know' + causative -ġül- + -n, Ming 敎知 'cause to know'), so 'without informing'. ečineġün (Ming 暗地行 'in a dark place') is 'secretly', related to ečine 'behind'; the ending is unclear. Qasar-un irge in-ü abču: 'Qasar's people, his, taking' — in-ü 'his' is Qasar's. Mother is the one kept in the dark.

sentences.t: Qasar-a miṅγan dörben žaγ̇ud irge ögbe.

morph.gloss: Qasar, a man’s name [人名 行]
people, subjects (Ming 百姓; the form of irgen) [百姓]

sentences.l: Qasar-to one thousand four hundreds people gave.
sentences.i: and gave Qasar fourteen hundred people.
sentences.n: Qasar-a 'to Qasar'; the number is miṅγan dörben žaγ̇ud, 'one thousand, four hundreds' (1400), with the same frame as the gifts of §242. So after this, Qasar has fourteen hundred; before the quarrel his share was four thousand (§242).

sentences.t: Eke medežü tere sedkil-dür ötör dötölegsen josun teimü.

morph.gloss: to cut across, take a short cut (stem inferred from the Ming 抄直; uncertain) [抄直了的]
custom, reason, the right way [道理]

sentences.l: Mother knowing, that heart-in quickly short-cut-having-taken reason so.
sentences.i: Mother knew of it, and in her heart she quickly took the short way: such was the reason.
sentences.n: medežü 'knowing', tere sedkil-dür 'in that heart' (Ming 心 裏). ötör is 'quickly' (Ming 快疾); dötölegsen is the active past participle (-gsen) of dötöle-, a stem I infer from the Ming 抄直 'cut straight across, short-cut' (the subject is Mother, not an unnamed thing 'cut short'); josun teimü is 'the way is so' (josun 'custom, reason, the way'; teimü 'thus'). Most doubtful unit of the part: I cannot give a clear meaning to ötör dötölegsen; the Ming suggests a quick decision in Mother's heart, and `i` keeps the plain words, including josun 'reason', rather than force a reading.

sentences.t: Žalairtai Žebke tende γulažižu Barγužin oron buruγ̇udba.

morph.gloss: the Jalairtai, a people (Ming 種名; ending uncertain) [種(名)]
to bolt, run out in alarm (stem inferred from the Ming 驚出) [驚出着]
to flee, run away (Ming 逃走) [逃走了]

sentences.l: Žalairtai Žebke then startled-out Barγužin entering fled.
sentences.i: Then Jebke of the Jalairtai bolted in alarm, entered Barqujin and fled.
sentences.n: Žalairtai is a people (Ming 種(名)); I keep its -tai ending as part of the name. γulažižu is a converb with a stem γulaži- inferred from the Ming 驚出着 'startled and run out'; oron 'entering' is oro- + -n, and Barγužin is a place name (Ming 地名). buruγ̇udba 'fled' (Ming 逃走了). This Jebke is presumably the man assigned to Qasar in §243; his flight is the part's last event, and the Mongol does not say why he is alarmed.
